premises.authority: NIST SP 1065 source formula and Chez independent executable donor
NumPy reference + independent arithmetic research tests; application donor sources are motivations only

selected.law: For N zero-dead-time uniformly sampled fractional-frequency observations y, positive integer m and N >= 3m, average each m-point contiguous block: a_i=(1/m)*sum(y[i:i+m]); compute the mean squared second difference of consecutive m-block averages divided by 6, over all i=0..N-3m. Return exact rational variance when inputs are exact rational. Reject invalid m or insufficient data.

positive_witnesses.explanation: block means 0,1,0; m=2 reflects averaging time
linear frequency drift annihilated by second differences

falsifiers: Use the Allan first-difference estimator instead of the Hadamard second-difference estimator: a linear frequency drift becomes nonzero, violating the contract.
Normalize by 2 instead of 6, or silently use sample variance N-1; the 3-sample impulse must equal exactly 1/6.
Allow m=0, negative/non-integer m, N<3*m or silently fill missing samples; valid samples must be uniformly timed with no dead-time.
Conflate the HVAR finite nonoverlapping/overlapping convention or claim a different confidence estimator (modified or total Hadamard) is the same statistic.
selected.behavioral_independence: Hadamard exact second difference has zero response to linear fractional-frequency drift, unlike Allan first difference; do not conflate overlapping estimator conventions
selected.source_oracle: 15 previously recorded Chez oracle cases; not current SENS runtime proof

selected.law: For nonempty length n,m produce n+m-1 coefficients c[k]=Σ_i a[i]*b[k−i], treating out-of-bounds as zero; if either input empty the result is empty.
falsifiers: Cyclic convolution wraps the final coefficient into the first sample.
Cross-correlation fails reversing kernel where required by convolution.
Output shape differs from n+m-1 for nonempty inputs.
selected.behavioral_independence: Full linear exact convolution with n+m-1 coefficient law, unlike filtering/vector access or rational resampling using an explicitly supplied convolution substep.
selected.source_oracle: Existing exhaustive bounded Fraction models and independent coefficient/jump invariants; SENS runtime not established

selected.law: q[0]=p[0]; for each next i choose Δ congruent to (p[i]-p[i-1]) modulo period minimizing |Δ|; for exact half-period ties preserve the sign of the original raw difference; q[i]=q[i-1]+Δ. Empty input yields empty. This is local minimal-jump phase reconstruction, not a proof of physical phase trajectory.
falsifiers: Replacing the entire sequence with input modulo period loses accumulated revolutions.
For adjacent raw differences inside half period, altering values violates continuity law.
Half-period ties picked without stated rule make result nondeterministic.
selected.behavioral_independence: Canonical minimal adjacent unwrapping with specified half-period tie polarity and accumulation, not residue-class, physical ground-truth motion or one-modulus bounded inverse image.
selected.source_oracle: Existing exhaustive bounded Fraction models and independent coefficient/jump invariants; SENS runtime not established
